threads.body: This records `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` as `0` whenever `usage_metadata` exists but the keys are absent, which can silently fabricate token usage and produce misleading telemetry (and may also cause tests to treat missing-vs-zero incorrectly). Prefer only setting these fields when the corresponding keys are present (e.g., check key membership), or use `None` to represent unknown/missing.

threads.body: The truthiness check treats `0` the same as a missing value. If a provider reports `0` tokens (or the instrumentation assigns `0` as a default), this test will incorrectly expect the attribute to be absent. Use an explicit `is not None` / key-existence check to distinguish missing from zero.

threads.body: `raw` is assumed to be a `str`, but `metadata` is typed as `dict[str, Any]`. If `ls_provider` is ever non-string (or unhashable), `_PROVIDER_NAME_OVERRIDES.get(raw, raw)` can raise at runtime. Guard with `isinstance(raw, str)` and return `None` (or `str(raw)` if you explicitly want coercion).
